notes: University-administered merit scholarships (US$5,000-$35,000/yr, renewable 4 years) plus need-based aid for international undergraduates at Trinity University, San Antonio. Official page trinity.edu/admissions/aid/types/international states: 'International students are eligible for merit scholarships and need-based financial aid' and 'All international applicants are considered for general merit-based scholarships based on the materials submitted with their application for admission.' EducationUSA listing confirms 'Scholarships are automatically awarded at the time of admission. There is no separate application for scholarships.' Awarded by the Office of Admissions/Student Financial Services on academic profile; no faculty supervisor is attached to the award.

Johnson & Wales University invitation-based full-tuition scholarship for new F-1 international undergraduates. Official JWU page jwu.edu/admissions-aid/cost-aid/scholarships-grants-loans states: 'Every student is automatically considered for JWU merit scholarships with no separate application required.' Per the EducationUSA listing, candidates must be invited to apply through the JWU Admissions Portal and submit the Global Impact Statement plus two letters of recommendation. Selection is run by JWU Admissions/Student Financial Services; no supervising professor is attached to the award.

Singapore Ministry of Education awards-and-scholarships index (moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/awards-scholarships: 'Learn about the different merit-based awards and scholarships available.') spanning Centennial Fund Award, Edusave awards, MOE Pre-University Scholarship, MOE-AU Scholarship, ASEAN Scholarship and others. National government scheme with no single attached institution and no supervising professor; enquiries go to the ministry/MOE_AU_Scholarship@moe.gov.sg programme mailbox rather than to faculty.

Open Request for Research Proposals under SA-TIED phase 3 run by UNU-WIDER with the South African National Treasury; pays an honorarium of US$3,000-10,000 for a 10,000-word working paper to independent researchers/teams - research grant funding, not a supervised degree position. Official RfRP page publishes programme mailboxes only: questions to researchproposal3@wider.unu.edu and administrative/academic support to magrobi@wider.unu.edu. The SA-TIED team page (sa-tied.wider.unu.edu/team) names workstream academic and policy leads - Prof. Jukka Pirttila (Professor of Public Economics, University of Helsinki) and Prof. Nadine Riedel (Director, Institute for Public and Regional Economics, University of Munster) for public revenue mobilisation, and Prof. Murray Leibbrandt (University of Cape Town) with Dr Joshua Budlender (SALDRU, University of Cape Town) for poverty, inequality and labour markets - but these are programme-level leads who review/steer the workstreams, not supervisors of grantees, so no supervising professor is recorded.

Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship is a U.S. Department of Energy federal fellowship placing K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or Congressional offices (sponsoring agencies include DOE, the Library of Congress and USGS). It is not a degree programme and carries no university supervision; the official science.osti.gov/wdts/einstein page lists only the programme mailbox sc.einstein@doe.gov (a program office address, not a professor page).

notes: SCGSR is a supplemental award for thesis-based PhD students to conduct dissertation research at a DOE laboratory in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist. The official programme page publishes a 'running list of scientists... who are ready to collaborate with SCGSR awardees' with their institutional e-mail addresses; three are listed here as examples of potential collaborating supervisors (the full list on the page is longer). Application also requires coordination with the awardee's own PhD thesis advisor at the home graduate institution.

Chevening SIDS Scholarship is a UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) government scholarship for applicants from Commonwealth Small Island Developing States to pursue a one-year master's degree at any eligible UK university of their choice. Per chevening.org/sids-chevening-scholarship it 'is an opportunity for outstanding individuals from Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to pursue a one-year master's degree in the UK' - no institution or supervising professor is attached at award stage, so the scheme is not applicable for supervisor enrichment. (Note: the description field in the batch input about the French Community of Belgium/Quebec does not match the official source and appears to be a data error.)
